# Setup: RStudio in your Browser {.unnumbered}

In this module you use **RStudio in your web browser**. You don't need to install anything. R, RStudio and all the course files are ready for you.

This works on any computer: university PCs, Windows laptops, Macs and Chromebooks.

It runs on **GitHub Codespaces**. A *codespace* is your own computer on the internet. Only you can use it, and it keeps your files between sessions.

## 1. First time only

**Step 1. Make a GitHub account.**

Go to [github.com/signup](https://github.com/signup) and create a free account. You can use your university email. Then sign in.

**Step 2. Create your codespace.**

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
Click this button, then click the green **Create codespace** button:

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/GDSL-UL/stats?quickstart=1)
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="html"}
Open this link, then click the green **Create codespace** button:

<https://codespaces.new/GDSL-UL/stats?quickstart=1>
:::

Wait while your codespace is built. **The first time this takes several minutes**, because R, RStudio and the course packages are installed for you. Don't close the tab. (Next time it opens much faster.)

When it's ready, a blue and grey window opens in your browser. This is called VS Code. **You don't need to use it**, but keep it open in the background.

**Step 3. Open RStudio.**

When everything is ready, you have two ways to open RStudio:

-   A small message appears in the bottom-right corner. Click **Open in Browser**.
-   Or look at the panel at the bottom of the window. Find the box that says **RStudio is ready**. Hold Ctrl (Cmd on a Mac) and click the link in the box.

RStudio opens in a new tab.

::: callout-tip
**The new tab is stuck on a GitHub page that says "authenticating"?** This is normal. Try these in order:

1.  Press F5 to refresh the page.
2.  Wait a minute: RStudio may still be starting. Then refresh again.
3.  Use a normal browser window, not a private or incognito one. Chrome or Edge work best. Some browsers (Safari, Brave, or Firefox/Edge with strict tracking protection) block the cookie GitHub needs to sign you in: allow cookies for `github.dev` or switch browser.
4.  In the VS Code window, click the **Ports** tab in the bottom panel, right-click the **RStudio** row (port 8787) and choose **Open in Browser**.
:::

**Step 4. Bookmark the RStudio tab.**

This is your personal RStudio address. Use it to come back quickly next time.

## 2. Every time you work

1.  Go to [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces) and click your codespace. You can also click the button in Step 2 again: it takes you back to the codespace you already have.
2.  Open RStudio with your bookmark, or as in Step 3.
3.  Work in the RStudio tab.
4.  When you finish, go back to [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces). Click the **...** next to your codespace and choose **Stop codespace**. This saves your free hours. Your files are not deleted. If you forget, it stops by itself after about an hour without using RStudio.

## 3. Your files

In RStudio, the **Files** panel (bottom right) shows the course folder:

```
stats/
├── data/    the datasets
├── img/     pictures used in the labs
├── labs/    one lab file for each week
└── myLabs/  your own copies of the labs: you work here
```

Everything is already in the right place. **You don't need to download, move or set up anything.**

The `labs` folder updates automatically each time you open your codespace, so you always have the latest version of the labs. **Don't work in the files in `labs`:** if you change one, the whole `labs` folder can stop updating. Work on your own copy in `myLabs` instead (see below). Nothing in `myLabs` is ever changed or replaced.

## 4. Your first lab (Week 1)

1.  In the **Files** panel, click `labs`, then click `00.introR.qmd`. The lab opens in the top-left panel. It shows you around RStudio and how to run code.
2.  **Make your own copy.** Click `File -> Save As...`, go to the `myLabs` folder, and click **Save**. The copy is now open in RStudio: work in this one.
3.  Then open `01.DataExploration.qmd` from `labs` and copy it to `myLabs` in the same way. This is the main practical for Week 1.
4.  Go through each lab from top to bottom and run each code chunk. Write your notes and answers in the white space between the chunks.
5.  Save often: press Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on a Mac).

Each week, open that week's lab from `labs`, save a copy in `myLabs`, and work on the copy. Next time, open your copy straight from `myLabs`.

Your changes are only saved in your own codespace. They don't change the website, and other students can't see them.

::: callout-note
**How the labs find the data**

The lab code loads data like this:

```{r}
#| eval: false
attacks <- read.csv("../data/attacksUK.csv")
```

`../` means "go up one folder". Your copy of the lab is in `myLabs`, so R goes up to `stats` and then into `data`. You don't need to change these lines.
:::

## 5. Adding data from Canvas

Some datasets are only on Canvas, for example the Family Resource Survey (FRS). To add one:

1.  Download the file from Canvas to your computer.
2.  In RStudio's **Files** panel, click `data`.
3.  If the lab asks for a new folder (for example `FRS`), click **New Folder**, type the name, and click **OK**. Then click the new folder to open it.
4.  Click **Upload**, then **Choose File**. Pick the file you downloaded and click **OK**.

Now the lab code will find the file.

## 6. Saving a copy on your computer

To download a file from RStudio (for example to keep a copy, or to submit your work):

1.  In the **Files** panel, tick the box next to the file.
2.  Click **More**, then **Export...**, then **Download**.

For the assessment, download the report template from Canvas and upload it to your `myLabs` folder (the same way as in section 5). Write your report there. You submit an `.html` file, which you make with the **Render** button at the top of your file. See [How to submit](howSubmit.qmd).

::: callout-warning
**Keep copies of your work.** If you don't open your codespace for 30 days, GitHub deletes it, and your files are deleted too. Download your files from `myLabs` from time to time, and always before holidays and before the assessment deadline.
:::

## 7. If something goes wrong

-   **RStudio is stuck on "authenticating".** Press F5 to refresh the page. If that doesn't help, see the tips in Step 3 of section 1.
-   **RStudio says it lost the connection.** First press F5 to refresh the RStudio tab: often the connection just dropped for a moment, and your work is still there. If that doesn't help, your codespace has stopped. Open it again from [github.com/codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces), then refresh the RStudio tab.
-   **You don't see the `myLabs` folder.** Your codespace was created before we added it. In the VS Code window, click in the panel at the bottom, type `git pull` and press Enter. Then stop your codespace and open it again (see section 2).
-   **R says it can't find a file.** Check that the file is really in the folder named in the code. You can see this in the **Files** panel.
-   **GitHub says you have no free hours left.** The free plan gives you about 60 hours a month. Always stop your codespace when you finish (see section 2). If you run out, use RStudio on a university PC (see [Setup: RStudio on a PC or Laptop](localSetup.qmd)).

## Another option: RStudio on a university PC or your own laptop

You can also work in RStudio installed on a university PC or on your own laptop. See [Setup: RStudio on a PC or Laptop](localSetup.qmd).
